name: ServiceNow → DevRev migration POC
description: Parallel-run DevRev environment for a ServiceNow customer. ServiceNow Incidents become DevRev tickets, Change Requests and Problems become issues, CMDB configuration items map to the parts hierarchy (product → capability → feature), and the Service Catalog becomes KB articles. Assignment Groups become DevRev groups. The AirSync snap-in keeps both systems in sync during the parallel-run period.

plug_config.welcome_message: IT Service Desk — powered by DevRev. How can we help you today?
plug_config.ai_grounding_notes: This is an internal IT service desk. Users are employees reporting IT issues. Incidents are urgent operational problems; change requests need CAB approval; problems are root cause investigations. Refer to our KB articles for self-service steps before escalating.

ui_guidance.title: Map ServiceNow priority/impact to DevRev priority
steps: ServiceNow P1 (Critical) → DevRev p0 — major outage or security breach affecting business operations.
ServiceNow P2 (High) → DevRev p1 — significant impact on a team or service, workaround available.
ServiceNow P3 (Moderate) → DevRev p2 — limited impact, non-urgent.
ServiceNow P4/P5 (Low/Planning) → DevRev p3 — cosmetic issues, low-priority requests.
ServiceNow uses a priority matrix (Impact × Urgency). DevRev uses a single priority field. Use the Impact value as the primary driver when collapsing.
The 'major-incident' tag is added to any p0 ticket migrated from ServiceNow to flag it for major incident review in DevRev.

ui_guidance.title: Map ServiceNow tables to DevRev work types
steps: ServiceNow Incident (incident table) → DevRev ticket (use the 'incident' tag).
ServiceNow Change Request (change_request table) → DevRev issue (use the 'change-request' tag). Change requests are planned work, not reactive support.
ServiceNow Problem (problem table) → DevRev issue (use the 'problem' tag). Problems track root cause investigations.
ServiceNow Service Catalog requests → DevRev ticket for end-user-facing requests, or issue for IT-internal requests.
ServiceNow Task (sys_task subtable) → DevRev issue linked to its parent incident/change via 'is_dependent_on'.
ServiceNow Event (em_event table) → DevRev incident (for major event correlation and P0 outage tracking).

ui_guidance.title: Map ServiceNow CMDB to DevRev parts hierarchy
steps: ServiceNow Application Service (top-level CMDB CI class) → DevRev product.
ServiceNow CI Class (e.g., Network, Server, Software) → DevRev capability under the relevant product.
Individual ServiceNow CIs (e.g., specific servers, apps) that need work tracking → DevRev feature under the matching capability.
Not every CI needs to be a part — only ones with recurring incidents or change requests benefit from the hierarchy.
Use this blueprint's parts hierarchy as a starting template. Adjust capability and feature names to match your CMDB CI classes before applying.

ui_guidance.title: Map ServiceNow workflow states to DevRev stages
steps: This blueprint creates five custom stages to complement DevRev's built-in pipeline.
ServiceNow New/Open → DevRev backlog.
ServiceNow In Progress (assigned) → DevRev in_development.
ServiceNow On Hold (awaiting approval) → DevRev Pending Approval (custom stage, ordinal 120).
ServiceNow In Review / Awaiting Change → DevRev In Review (custom stage, ordinal 250).
ServiceNow On Hold (awaiting vendor) → DevRev Pending Vendor (custom stage, ordinal 350).
ServiceNow On Hold (awaiting user) → DevRev Pending User (custom stage, ordinal 450).
ServiceNow Resolved → DevRev Resolved (custom stage, ordinal 850).
ServiceNow Closed → DevRev completed (built-in closed state).
After applying, go to Settings → Object Customization → Stage Diagrams to configure allowed transitions.

ui_guidance.title: Importing your ServiceNow export
steps: Export incidents from ServiceNow: Navigate to Incident → All → Export → CSV.
Useful columns to include: Number, Short description, Description, Priority, State, Assignment group, Assigned to, Category, Subcategory, Opened at, Resolved at, Configuration item.
Export change requests: Navigate to Change → All → Export → CSV. Include: Number, Short description, Type (Normal/Emergency/Standard), Risk, State, Assignment group, CAB date.
Drop each CSV next to this blueprint and add a `csv` entry: `{ "path": "./incidents.csv", "entity": "tickets" }` or `"issues"` for change requests.
Use `column_map` to remap ServiceNow column names — e.g., `{ "Short description": "title", "Priority": "priority", "Assignment group": "owned_by" }`.
For large exports (>1000 records), split by table type: incidents.csv, changes.csv, problems.csv.

ui_guidance.title: Assignment group to DevRev group migration
steps: ServiceNow assignment groups are mapped to DevRev groups in this blueprint: L1 Service Desk, L2 Infrastructure, L2 End-User Computing, L3 Security, Change Advisory Board.
After applying, invite the actual team members into each DevRev group via Settings → Groups.
For the CAB group, use DevRev's approval workflow on change-request issues to replicate the CAB approval gate.
If your org has additional assignment groups, add them to the 'groups' section of this blueprint before applying.

ui_guidance.title: SLA policy configuration
steps: This blueprint creates three SLA policies: Enterprise (Meridian), Standard (Commercial), and HIPAA Security (Altavance).
After applying, go to Settings → SLAs to assign each policy to the correct account or ticket category.
ServiceNow SLA timers pause when a ticket enters 'Pending User' or 'Pending Vendor' state — configure the same pause rules in DevRev's SLA settings.
HIPAA breach notification requires 60-day external reporting. Track this via a custom field on security incident tickets.
Adjust the first_response and resolution targets in this blueprint to match your existing ServiceNow SLA commitments before applying.

ui_guidance.title: Cutover and parallel-run playbook
steps: Week 1–2: Apply this blueprint, configure groups, and validate the part hierarchy matches your CMDB.
Week 3–4: Begin routing new incidents into DevRev while ServiceNow remains the system of record. Use DevRev's email channel or PLuG widget for inbound.
Week 5–6: Enable the AirSync snap-in (Settings → Integrations → Snap-ins → Install ServiceNow Airsync) for bidirectional sync of open incidents.
Authenticate AirSync with your ServiceNow instance URL, admin username, and password.
Map ServiceNow tables to DevRev object types in the AirSync configuration.
Cutover: Freeze new ticket creation in ServiceNow. Export and import the open-ticket delta CSV. Disable the AirSync sync. Announce DevRev as the system of record.
Post-cutover: Archive the ServiceNow instance or put it in read-only mode. Migrate historical reports to DevRev Insights.
